title: Optimistic Updates
outcome: Add optimistic UI safely by defining snapshot, optimistic state, rollback, reconciliation, temporary identity, and concurrency behavior.
artifact: Optimistic task update/create flow with rollback and authoritative server reconciliation.
labSteps: Choose one mutation where low failure probability and UX benefit justify optimism.
Capture the previous cache state before changing it.
Apply an optimistic update to the exact affected query data.
Force a server failure and prove rollback restores the previous state.
On success/settle, reconcile with authoritative server data rather than trusting the optimistic object forever.
Simulate two rapid mutations and reason about race ordering and stale responses.
failureModes: Temporary IDs colliding with real IDs
Older mutation response overwriting newer user intent
Optimistically updating the wrong filtered list
mastery: Can decide when optimism is inappropriate
principles: Optimistic updates must define how to snapshot, apply, roll back, and reconcile state.
Use optimism where failure is uncommon and the user benefit justifies rollback complexity.
Handle concurrent mutations and stale responses so an older result cannot overwrite newer user intent.
Always reconcile optimistic client state with authoritative server state.
